title: One-loop SU(Nc) Yang–Mills running
question: Does direct fourth-order Runge–Kutta integration of the one-loop SU(Nc) beta function reproduce the independently integrated inverse-coupling relation on fixed positive RG-time samples?

theory.object: Four-dimensional SU(Nc) Yang–Mills theory with Nf massless Dirac fermions in the fundamental representation, restricted to the one-loop running-coupling ODE.
theory.signature: Minkowski (-,+,+,+); the running equation is an RG-time ODE and is signature-independent at this level.
theory.units: Natural units hbar=c=1. The gauge coupling and t=ln(mu/mu0) are dimensionless.
assumptions: Nc is a positive integer and Nf is a nonnegative integer with b0=(11Nc-2Nf)/3>0.
Massless fundamental fermions; beta(g)=-b0*g^3/(16*pi^2), with no higher-loop terms.
Initial coupling g0=0.8 (alpha0=g0^2/(4*pi), perturbatively small); fixed positive RG times; no thresholds or changes of active Nf.
This equation and its numerical solution are a teaching example, not a fitted or phenomenological QCD prediction.
theory.boundary_conditions: g(t=0)=g0=0.8, evaluated at t=ln(mu/mu0) in {0.25,1,4,8}; no threshold crossing is included.
theory.observable: The dimensionless running coupling g(t) obtained by RK4 integration of dg/dt=-b0*g^3/(16*pi^2), compared pointwise with the integrated one-loop expression g(t)=[g0^-2+b0*t/(8*pi^2)]^-1/2.
theory.regulator: None: this finite-dimensional ODE example has no UV or IR regulator.
theory.limit_order: None; no continuum or perturbative-order limit is computed beyond declaring the one-loop truncation.
theory.normalization: t=ln(mu/mu0), beta(g)=dg/dt, and the conventional one-loop coefficient b0=11Nc/3-2Nf/3 for fundamental Dirac fermions.

claim.statement: For the listed asymptotically-free SU(Nc) parameter cases and positive RG times, direct RK4 integration agrees with the one-loop inverse-coupling solution within the predeclared numerical-error gates.
claim.scope: A deterministic educational ODE cross-check for Nc=3, Nf in {0,3,6}, g0=0.8, the fixed time grid and RK4 step refinement recorded in calculation.py.
limitations: The closed-form comparison independently integrates the same declared one-loop beta function; it is not an independent derivation of that beta coefficient.
No higher-loop running, scheme conversion, matching, quark-mass effects, threshold crossing, or experimental data are included.
Finite sampled agreement is not a theorem about arbitrary initial data or all RG times.
forbidden_inferences: Do not present this as a real-QCD prediction, a precision determination of alpha_s, a measurement, or evidence for nonperturbative confinement.
Do not infer numerical agreement proves the beta-function coefficient or an all-orders statement.

sources.revision: Published 25 June 1973; Crossref metadata queried for DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.30.1343.
sources.locator: Bibliographic metadata and title/abstract-level public description only; full article not read for this example.

protocol.disconfirming: A failed numerical threshold means this fixed-grid implementation did not meet its predeclared ODE agreement gate; it does not disconfirm asymptotic freedom or the one-loop formula globally.
protocol.independence: The beta function, parameters and physical definition are shared. The ODE value is obtained by direct RK4 stepping; the comparator is obtained by analytically integrating d(1/g^2)/dt. These are distinct numerical/analytic implementations, not two independent derivations of the underlying theory or beta coefficient.
protocol.failure_interpretation: A script error, invalid output or failed metric is an implementation/numerical-gate failure. A passing result checks this finite educational computation only and does not promote the exploratory claim status.
